title: Hepatocellular Carcinoma
subtitle: StewardMD ONCOTREE navigator (draft)
provenanceNote: DRAFT decision support authored from standard guidelines (NCCN/DeVita/Harrison) - physician decides. Pathway: workup -> diagnostic confirmation -> Child-Pugh + performance status -> BCLC stage -> stage-directed arms (resection / ablation / transplant / TACE / radioembolization / systemic by line) -> recurrence and surveillance. The one leaf with a matching StewardMD dose protocol (sorafenib) references it; all other modalities and agents are shown as checklist guidance with NO dose. Workup, staging and surveillance wording is standard oncology, not proprietary guideline text. Invents no dose/regimen. DRAFT - not clinically activated.
sourceNote: Structural pathway consistent with Standard Guidelines (NCCN/BCLC) for hepatocellular carcinoma. Regimen options reference existing StewardMD Standard Protocols where available; the dose engine computes patient doses.

a.text: Atezolizumab + bevacizumab is a preferred first-line option for advanced disease in Child-Pugh A patients with adequate performance status; screen for and manage esophageal varices before starting because of bleeding risk with the anti-VEGF component.

b.text: Systemic therapy data are strongest in Child-Pugh A. Child-Pugh B is under-represented in trials; treat selectively with close monitoring and avoid in decompensated (Child-Pugh C) liver disease.

c.text: In an at-risk cirrhotic liver, a nodule with the characteristic arterial hyperenhancement plus washout pattern on multiphasic CT/MRI (LI-RADS 5) can establish the diagnosis without biopsy; biopsy is reserved for indeterminate lesions.

d.text: Transplant candidacy is generally judged against accepted size/number thresholds (e.g. Milan criteria); tumors beyond criteria may be considered for downstaging before listing.

nodes.name: Initial workup
nodes.title: Initial workup and baseline assessment
nodes.description: Baseline evaluation before staging: confirm the lesion, characterize liver function, and assess extent.

bullets.label: History, physical, performance status; assess cirrhosis etiology
Liver function: bilirubin, albumin, INR, ascites and encephalopathy for Child-Pugh; consider ALBI grade
Serum AFP (baseline and for later trend)
Multiphasic contrast CT or MRI of the liver; chest CT for extent
Assess portal vein for tumor thrombus and screen for extrahepatic spread
Upper endoscopy to screen for varices if portal hypertension or before anti-VEGF therapy
Viral hepatitis serologies and antiviral therapy planning

nodes.name: Presentation
nodes.title: Clinical presentation / care phase
nodes.description: Select the current clinical situation to enter the correct pathway.

nodes.name: Diagnostic confirmation
nodes.title: Confirming the diagnosis
nodes.description: In an at-risk cirrhotic liver, imaging alone can confirm HCC; otherwise biopsy is needed.
bullets: Characteristic arterial hyperenhancement with washout (LI-RADS 5) in a cirrhotic liver is diagnostic
Biopsy for indeterminate lesions or a non-cirrhotic liver

nodes.name: Tissue / repeat imaging
nodes.title: Indeterminate lesion: biopsy or short-interval re-imaging
nodes.description: Resolve the diagnosis before committing to cancer-directed therapy.
bullets: Image-guided core biopsy of the indeterminate lesion
Alternatively short-interval repeat multiphasic imaging to reassess LI-RADS category
Re-enter staging once the diagnosis is established

nodes.name: Liver function / PS
nodes.title: Child-Pugh class and performance status
nodes.description: Underlying liver reserve and performance status constrain every treatment decision in HCC.

options.label: Child-Pugh C or poor PS / decompensated

nodes.name: Supportive care / transplant eval
nodes.title: Decompensated or terminal: supportive care (transplant if eligible)
nodes.description: Child-Pugh C or terminal-stage disease: prioritize liver-directed transplant evaluation where feasible, otherwise best supportive care.
bullets: Liver transplant evaluation if tumor burden and candidacy allow (best option for decompensated cirrhosis with limited tumor)
Otherwise best supportive / palliative care and symptom control
Manage ascites, encephalopathy and nutrition; hepatology co-management
Systemic anticancer therapy is generally not appropriate in Child-Pugh C

nodes.name: BCLC stage
nodes.title: BCLC stage
nodes.description: Assign the Barcelona Clinic Liver Cancer stage from tumor burden, vascular invasion / spread, and performance status.

tables.title: BCLC stage summary (simplified)
rows: Single, or up to 3 nodules <= 3 cm, no vascular invasion
Portal vein tumor thrombus and/or extrahepatic spread

nodes.name: Early-stage choice
nodes.title: BCLC 0 / A: curative-intent option
nodes.description: Choose among curative options by resectability, liver reserve, portal hypertension, and transplant candidacy.

bullets.label: Resection
bullets.sub: single tumor, preserved function, no clinically significant portal hypertension

bullets.label: Ablation
bullets.sub: small tumor(s) <= 3 cm, not a surgical candidate or as an alternative to resection

bullets.label: Transplant
bullets.sub: within accepted criteria, especially with impaired liver function

bullets.label: Downstaging / bridging
bullets.sub: beyond criteria but a potential transplant candidate

nodes.name: Resection
nodes.title: Surgical resection
nodes.description: Preferred curative option for a single resectable tumor with preserved liver function and no significant portal hypertension.
bullets: Anatomic partial hepatectomy with adequate future liver remnant
Confirm no significant portal hypertension and Child-Pugh A function
Continue antiviral therapy for viral hepatitis to protect the remnant
Enter structured surveillance after resection

nodes.name: Transplant
nodes.title: Liver transplantation
nodes.description: Curative for early HCC within accepted criteria, treating both tumor and underlying cirrhosis.
bullets: List if within accepted size/number criteria (e.g. Milan)
Bridging therapy (ablation, TACE or radioembolization) to prevent dropout while waiting
Preferred over resection when liver function is impaired
Lifelong immunosuppression and post-transplant surveillance

nodes.name: Ablation
nodes.title: Local ablation
nodes.description: Curative-intent for small tumors, especially when surgery is not suitable.
bullets: Radiofrequency or microwave ablation for tumors up to about 3 cm
Comparable to resection for very small tumors in non-surgical candidates
Consider combining with TACE for tumors in the 3-5 cm range
Enter structured surveillance after ablation

nodes.name: Downstaging / bridging
nodes.title: Downstaging toward transplant / resection
nodes.description: Tumor beyond transplant criteria in an otherwise eligible patient: locoregional therapy to shrink burden into criteria.
bullets: TACE or radioembolization (Y90) to reduce tumor burden
Re-stage on response; list for transplant once within criteria
Enforce a defined observation interval before listing to select favorable biology
Reassess resectability if response is deep

nodes.name: Intermediate choice
nodes.title: BCLC B: locoregional vs systemic
nodes.description: Intermediate, liver-confined multinodular disease: select locoregional therapy or move to systemic if unsuitable / TACE-refractory.

bullets.label: TACE
bullets.sub: preserved function, liver-confined, amenable arterial supply

bullets.label: Systemic
bullets.sub: diffuse / bulky bilobar disease or TACE-refractory / TACE-unsuitable

nodes.name: TACE
nodes.title: Transarterial chemoembolization (TACE)
nodes.description: Standard first choice for intermediate-stage, liver-confined multinodular HCC.
bullets: Selective / superselective delivery to preserve non-tumor parenchyma
Repeat on-demand for viable disease; reassess response by imaging
Move to systemic therapy on TACE refractoriness or when further TACE would harm liver function
Continue liver-function monitoring between sessions

nodes.name: Radioembolization
nodes.title: Transarterial radioembolization (Y90)
nodes.description: Selective internal radiation for suitable intermediate-stage disease or as a bridging / downstaging tool.
bullets: Pre-treatment mapping angiography and lung-shunt assessment
Lobar or segmental (radiation-segmentectomy) delivery
Option for bridging / downstaging toward transplant or resection
Monitor liver function after treatment

nodes.name: Systemic line
nodes.title: Systemic therapy: line of therapy
nodes.description: For advanced / progressing disease with preserved liver function, choose the line based on prior systemic exposure.
bullets: Systemic therapy is for Child-Pugh A (selected B) with adequate performance status
Sequencing depends on the first-line agent already used

nodes.name: First-line choice
nodes.title: First-line systemic selection
nodes.description: Select the first-line backbone by immunotherapy eligibility and bleeding / autoimmune contraindications.

bullets.label: Atezolizumab + bevacizumab
bullets.sub: preferred if no contraindication; screen/treat varices first

nodes.name: Atezo + bev
nodes.title: First line: atezolizumab + bevacizumab
nodes.description: Preferred first-line regimen for advanced HCC in Child-Pugh A patients without contraindications.
bullets: Confirm Child-Pugh A and adequate performance status
Endoscopy to screen for and manage varices before starting (bevacizumab bleeding risk)
Monitor for immune-related adverse events and proteinuria / hypertension
No StewardMD dose protocol here yet - shown as guidance; physician arranges the regimen

nodes.name: Durva + treme
nodes.title: First line: durvalumab + tremelimumab (dual immunotherapy)
nodes.description: First-line dual immune checkpoint option, useful when the anti-VEGF component of atezo-bev is contraindicated.
bullets: Single priming dose of tremelimumab added to durvalumab, then durvalumab maintenance (STRIDE-type schedule)
Avoids bevacizumab bleeding risk; no mandatory variceal screening for the anti-VEGF reason
Monitor for immune-related adverse events
No StewardMD dose protocol here yet - shown as guidance; physician arranges the regimen

nodes.name: First-line TKI
nodes.title: First-line TKI selection
nodes.description: When immunotherapy is contraindicated, choose the oral multikinase inhibitor.

nodes.name: Lenvatinib
nodes.title: First line: lenvatinib
nodes.description: Oral multikinase inhibitor, non-inferior first-line TKI alternative to sorafenib.
bullets: Weight-based dosing; monitor blood pressure and thyroid function
Often preferred over sorafenib for higher response rate
Confirm Child-Pugh A function
No StewardMD dose protocol here yet - shown as guidance; physician arranges the regimen

nodes.name: Sorafenib
nodes.title: First line: sorafenib
nodes.description: The reference first-line multikinase inhibitor for advanced HCC.
bullets: Monitor for hand-foot skin reaction, diarrhea, hypertension
Confirm Child-Pugh A function; dose modify for toxicity
Dose protocol referenced below

nodes.name: Second-line choice
nodes.title: Second-line systemic selection
nodes.description: After first-line progression, select by the prior agent and AFP level.

nodes.name: Regorafenib
nodes.title: Second line: regorafenib (post-sorafenib)
nodes.description: For patients who tolerated and then progressed on sorafenib.
bullets: Indicated specifically after sorafenib tolerance and progression
Monitor for hand-foot skin reaction, hypertension, hepatotoxicity
Confirm Child-Pugh A function
No StewardMD dose protocol here yet - shown as guidance; physician arranges the regimen

nodes.name: Cabozantinib
nodes.title: Second / later line: cabozantinib
nodes.description: Multikinase inhibitor active after prior systemic therapy.
bullets: Option after progression on one or two prior systemic agents
Monitor for hand-foot skin reaction, diarrhea, hypertension
Confirm Child-Pugh A function
No StewardMD dose protocol here yet - shown as guidance; physician arranges the regimen

nodes.name: Ramucirumab
nodes.title: Second line: ramucirumab (AFP >= 400)
nodes.description: Anti-VEGFR2 antibody for patients with AFP at or above 400 ng/mL after first-line therapy.
bullets: Biomarker-selected: baseline AFP >= 400 ng/mL
Monitor for hypertension and proteinuria
Confirm Child-Pugh A function
No StewardMD dose protocol here yet - shown as guidance; physician arranges the regimen

nodes.name: Third line
nodes.title: Third line and beyond
nodes.description: Sequential single-agent therapy after two prior lines, or best supportive care.
bullets: Sequence a not-yet-used TKI (regorafenib / cabozantinib) or checkpoint inhibitor per prior exposure
Clinical trial where available
Reassess liver function and performance status before each new line
Transition to best supportive care when Child-Pugh declines or PS is poor

nodes.name: Recurrence
nodes.title: Recurrence after curative therapy
nodes.description: Recurrence after resection, ablation or transplant: re-stage and treat by pattern.
bullets: Re-image liver and chest; recheck AFP and liver function
Localized intrahepatic recurrence may be re-treated with curative or locoregional intent
Diffuse or extrahepatic recurrence is treated as advanced disease

nodes.name: Repeat local therapy
nodes.title: Localized recurrence: repeat local / locoregional therapy
nodes.description: Curative or locoregional re-treatment for isolated intrahepatic recurrence with preserved function.
bullets: Re-resection or ablation for isolated resectable / ablatable recurrence
Salvage transplant in selected candidates within criteria
TACE / radioembolization for multifocal but liver-confined recurrence
Resume surveillance after re-treatment

nodes.name: Surveillance
nodes.title: Post-treatment surveillance / follow-up
nodes.description: Monitoring cadence after curative or locoregional therapy; escalate on recurrence.
bullets: Multiphasic CT/MRI and AFP every 3-6 months for the first 2 years, then every 6-12 months
Ongoing screening of the cirrhotic remnant liver for new primaries
Continue antiviral therapy and hepatology co-management
A confirmed new lesion or rising AFP enters the recurrence pathway
